prompt.text:
Reference image 1 shows the chosen design of MAW ROCKET. Redraw the referenced subject as the sheet described below. Keep the exact design, silhouette, proportions, colour palette, materials, top-left lighting, outline weight and rendering style of the reference in every cell; only the pose or state changes from cell to cell, and the layout follows the grid described: Retro 16-bit video game sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shooter, a regular grid of four equal cells in two rows of two with even gutters, read left to right and top to bottom, every cell showing the same MAW ROCKET enemy — a small steel torpedo with a hinged open fish-jaw nose showing a dark throat, a finned steel body and an orange nozzle flame at the tail, side view facing left, at the same scale and position, on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background. The frames in order: four flame-flicker states of the tail nozzle on the identical torpedo body. Follow the established design exactly; only the pose or state changes between cells. Crisp pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, identical silhouette and palette in every cell, no anti-aliasing, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no numbers, no cell borders. The background is one perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key colour everywhere around the subject: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast or drop shadow, no glow or green spill on the subject. No text, letters, numbers, labels, UI or watermark anywhere.
 The torpedo with its open jaw is pixel-identical in all four cells; only the tail flame changes, clearly: short, medium, long, and medium with a forked tip. Only empty green space between the cells, no lines.
prompt.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, labels, numbers, cell borders, watermark, blurry, green tint on the subject, green spill
